intro: Lesson 116: Revision: C4 crude oil, alkanes and alkenes. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: (a) Describe how crude oil is separated into fractions [4]. (b) Describe a test to distinguish propane from propene, with results [3]. (c) Give the name of C₅H₁₂ [1].
questions.a: (a) crude oil heated/vaporised (1); vapour rises up column, cooler at top (1); fractions condense at their boiling points (1); short chains/low bp collected at top, long at bottom (1); (b) add bromine water and shake (1); propene: orange to colourless (1); propane: stays orange (1); (c) pentane (1)
questions.model: Teacher writes the first point: 'Crude oil is heated until most of it vaporises.'

questions.q: Write the equation for methane reacting with chlorine in UV light and name the type of reaction.
Explain why alkanes are called saturated.
questions.a: Each carbon has the maximum number of hydrogen atoms; only single bonds, no C=C.

questions.q: Draw the two structural isomers of C₄H₁₀ and name them.
questions.a: Butane (straight chain) (1); methylpropane (branched) (1); correct displayed formulae (1)
questions.model: Four carbons in a line: butane. Three in a line with one branching off the middle: methylpropane. Same formula, different structure.

questions.q: Write the equation for ethene with bromine.
Why does bitumen have a high boiling point?
questions.a: Long-chain molecules with strong intermolecular forces
